findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, but `order()` is added as a required abstract method. Any provider compiled against the previous interface (including third-party providers discovered through ServiceLoader) does not implement this method. Such providers will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` sorts providers, and source-compatible providers will no longer compile until updated. Make this a default method (with an appropriate default priority) or provide a compatibility path before invoking it.

findings.title: Equal provider priorities make crypto-provider selection classpath-order dependent
findings.body: Provider selection now silently chooses the first provider after sorting by `order()`, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same priority (200). For a classpath containing more than one of these providers, the comparator leaves ties in ServiceLoader discovery order, which depends on classpath/resource ordering rather than an explicit security policy. In particular, a deployment containing both FIPS1402Provider and DefaultCryptoProvider can silently select the non-FIPS provider instead of failing as it did previously, defeating the expected FIPS configuration. Assign unambiguous priorities or reject equal-priority candidates rather than selecting one arbitrarily.

findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key and do not exercise their signature encodings
findings.body: The test constructs one unspecified default EC key pair, which is normally P-256, and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. Consequently the ES384/ES512 cases only convert 32-byte P-256 R/S values padded to larger requested lengths; they do not exercise 48-byte ES384 values, 66-byte ES512 values, or the long-form DER sequence length that ES512 commonly requires. Generate keys on secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively (and ideally verify the reconstructed DER signature) so the tests cover the encoding paths claimed by each algorithm.
